accepted.title: Finite section-isomorphism orbits despite infinitely many homotopy classes
accepted.text: A Lefschetz fibration here is a smooth map π:X⁴→S² from a closed connected oriented4-manifold, with connected surface fibres and finitely many orientation-compatible complex Morse singularities z₁²+z₂², distinct critical values and relatively minimal fibres. Does there exist such a fibration with infinitely many homotopy classes of smooth sections but only finitely many isomorphism classes of sections? Can the number of isomorphism classes be1? Sections s₁,s₂ are isomorphic if there are orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms Ψ:X→X and ψ:S²→S² with π∘Ψ=ψ∘π and Ψ∘s₁=s₂∘ψ. Homotopy here is homotopy of the section maps S²→X.

accepted.title: Infinite families outside partial-conjugation equivalence
accepted.text: A Lefschetz fibration here is a smooth map π:X⁴→S² from a closed connected oriented4-manifold, with connected surface fibres and finitely many orientation-compatible complex Morse singularities z₁²+z₂², distinct critical values and relatively minimal fibres. Does there exist a fixed4-manifold X and an infinite family of Lefschetz fibrations X→S² of a common fibre genus such that no two are related by a finite sequence of partial conjugations and fibration equivalences? In monodromy terms, a partial conjugation replaces a contiguous subfactorization W₂ in W₁W₂=1 by its factorwise conjugate fW₂f⁻¹ when f commutes with the product W₂; usual Hurwitz moves and global conjugation encode fibration equivalence.
